research_references.authors: Sharada P. Mohanty, David P. Hughes, Marcel Salathé
research_references.title: Using Deep Learning for Image-Based Plant Disease Detection
research_references.relevant_findings: Demonstrated that deep convolutional networks achieve 99.35% accuracy on controlled lab images (PlantVillage), but model accuracy plummets to 31.4% when evaluated on field photographs under varying illumination and natural backgrounds. Emphasized that background shortcuts prevent true generalization to real-world farms.

research_references.title: Factors influencing the use of deep learning for plant disease recognition
research_references.relevant_findings: Identified that whole-leaf images suffer from severe confounding: leaf age, nutrient chlorosis look-alikes, multiple co-occurring diseases, and lighting glare. Emphasized the necessity of symptom-level analysis and structured metadata (growth stage, weather).

research_references.title: Plant disease identification from individual lesions and spots using deep learning
research_references.relevant_findings: Demonstrated that isolating and classifying individual lesions/spots significantly outperforms whole-image classification, particularly when distinguishing similar foliar diseases across solanaceous and cereal crops.

research_references.authors: Chuan Guo, Geoff Pleiss, Yu Sun, Kilian Q. Weinberger
research_references.title: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks
research_references.relevant_findings: Proved that modern deep architectures are miscalibrated and systematically overconfident. Raw softmax probabilities cannot be trusted as confidence scores. Recommended Temperature Scaling and Expected Calibration Error (ECE) monitoring for safety-critical deployment.

research_references.title: SelectiveNet: A Deep Neural Network with an Integrated Reject Option
research_references.relevant_findings: Formalized selective prediction in high-stakes classification: introducing a calibrated abstention mechanism ('Uncertain / Needs Extension Inspection') to maximize accuracy at target coverage levels, preventing catastrophic misdiagnosis.

research_references.authors: Dan Hendrycks, Mantas Mazeika, Thomas Dietterich
research_references.title: Deep Anomaly Detection with Outlier Exposure
research_references.relevant_findings: Demonstrated that Out-of-Distribution (OOD) inputs (such as non-plant images or unsupported crop varieties) produce dangerously high confidence in standard softmax heads unless explicitly calibrated with outlier exposure.

research_references.organization: Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) — National Research Centre for Integrated Pest Management (NCIPM)
research_references.title: Integrated Pest Management Packages for Major Horticultural & Field Crops
research_references.relevant_findings: Established Economic Threshold Levels (ETL), symptom progression charts, look-alike condition differentials (e.g., Cercospora vs Alternaria vs Bacterial spot), and the necessity of multi-parameter diagnostics combining plant part, crop stage, and weather history.

research_references.title: Vyavasaya Panchangam (Agricultural Almanac) & Crop Protection Recommendations
research_references.relevant_findings: Authoritative agronomic guidelines for Andhra Pradesh agro-climatic zones (Krishna-Godavari, Rayalaseema, North Coastal), defining localized seasonal outbreaks, chemical pre-harvest intervals (PHI), and resistant cultivar recommendations.

research_references.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
research_references.title: International Code of Conduct on Pesticide Management: Guidelines on Integrated Pest Management
research_references.relevant_findings: Defines the fundamental IPM decision pyramid: prevention and cultural suppression first, regular field scouting and ETL monitoring second, biological control third, and targeted chemical interventions strictly as a last resort.
